title: Founding a colony while standing in a thicket
question: Which of these reads as a colony that has actually taken hold in the undergrowth?
context_md:
Your playtest note, 2026-09-14: *"it should be easier to found a colony while standing in a thicket of plants."*

Same world, same seed, same stand, same frame. One press of the found-a-colony key in each.

**What was wrong.** Founding looked at the *soil* and wanted air directly above it. A forest floor never has that — it has root, stem base, grass blade, moss or fallen leaf — so a wood was the one place you could not start a colony. Censused on this world: 86 of 221 columns would take an ant in a grown wood, against 176 on bare ground, and every single refusal was a plant cell.

**What it does now.** It climbs through the plants to the first free cell, so an ant stands *on* the mat rather than being refused by it.

**The thing I cannot judge and you can.** Those ants are standing on grass and leaf, not on soil. I think that is right — the engine already lets an ant walk onto a leaf and treats a plant as something to stand on — but standing on foliage is exactly the kind of thing that is correct in the rules and looks like floating on screen. If it reads as floating, say so: the depth it will climb is one number and easy to pull back.

**Not in this picture, and worth knowing:** on a *fully* grown world this key still seats almost nobody, and that turned out to be nothing to do with plants — the world runs out of organism slots (4,095 of 4,095) and the game then says "no ground here", which is simply wrong. Filed separately as §Z21.

items.label: after
items.caption: a mat of plants counts as floor
